samples.question: The image shows three or four separate square patches of dark teal ink on a plain white background, well apart from one another. Inside each patch the teal ink is a set of thick cords folded into flat back-and-forth switchbacks: the cords are packed side by side and never touch or cross, and each patch is broken by exactly two short clear white gaps, so every patch holds exactly three separate cords. Exactly one patch also carries three small coloured square beads printed on its cords, one red, one blue and one yellow; ignore every other patch completely. Two beads count as lying on the same cord only when you can travel from one to the other along unbroken teal ink without crossing a white gap and without leaving the ink. Exactly two of the three beads lie on one shared cord and the remaining bead lies on a different cord. Straight-line distance across the white background is never a valid step. Which bead is the one that does not share its cord with either of the other two beads? Answer red, blue or yellow.
